title: A pinned passage clipped at the print width hides the anchor phrase of its tested question
goal: pack --root _self prints a pinned passage so that its tested question's anchor phrase is in the printed text: a passage longer than the clip is printed as the window around the phrase with an ellipsis at each cut end, so a tested question whose answer sits deep in a long single-sentence passage (the gate-options rule of backlog.md's Escalation line) is answered by the printed line and its row passes the eval

run: import subprocess,sys; out=subprocess.run(['python3','_tools/rag.py','pack','--root','_self','what must a gate about AGENTS.md or README.md state in each option'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout; sys.exit(0 if 'measured size' in out else 1)

gates.question: Who gets the key-word window: every clipped _self passage, or only a pinned one (then the repro needs the SS2-004 row or another tested question)?
options: every clipped _self passage (anchor phrase for a pinned one, else the densest cluster of the question key words): an unpinned weak pack hides its answer the same way, and the repro runs with no tested row
only a pinned passage, on its anchor phrase: other passages keep the head cut, and the repro needs a tested row
gates.recommendation: every clipped _self passage (anchor phrase for a pinned one, else the densest cluster of the question key words): an unpinned weak pack hides its answer the same way, and the repro runs with no tested row
gates.answer: every clipped _self passage (anchor phrase for a pinned one, else the densest cluster of the question key words): an unpinned weak pack hides its answer the same way, and the repro runs with no tested row

notes: Found by the review of ST-dvf3xf52: row SS2-004 of the skills' sets was left out of lookup_eval.csv because its pinned passage (backlog.md Escalation line, one sentence over the clip) prints without the phrase. The repro reads stdout only; the tool exits 0 on a pack, so a crash would show as a missing phrase too.
